messages:
marta-peopleops: Heads up: Lee submitted an accommodation request this morning. Manager Kevin separately flagged recent missed SLAs. Want to coordinate privately to align short-term support and avoid mixing medical details in public channels. Can @kevin-manager, @diego-engineering join a quick sync?

kevin-manager: Saw the intake link in my inbox. Not reviewed the docs. High-level: two sprints where several stories were delayed and a heated 1:1. I want to be supportive but also keep delivery on track. Recommend we agree on temporary task coverage before talking with Lee.

lee-ic: Thanks for the ping. I filed the request because shift changes and sleep disruption have made focused work hard lately. Id prefer any medical notes stay private. Happy to discuss adjustments.

diego-engineering: I can pick up the highest-priority incidents and cover the late release next week. Will coordinate handoff with Lee tonight.

kevin-manager: Appreciate that Diego. For scope: can we triage Lees open tickets and reassign blockers? If we can reduce immediate pressure, Id rather avoid formal performance escalation while accommodations are evaluated.

marta-peopleops: Plan: 1) PeopleOps will log the intake and assign an ADA coordinator; 2) temporary on-call reassign for 2 weeks; 3) shift recurring meeting times earlier where possible; 4) pause low-priority async tasks for the evaluation period. Diego to do on-call cover, Kevin to publish triage list. Ill schedule a private intake call for within 48 hours.

ada-bot: [automated] Accommodation intake case C-1935002222 opened for user lee-ic. Coordinator: marta-peopleops. Intake call target: 2 business days. Reminder: keep medical attachments out of open channels.

kevin-manager: Ill DM the triage spreadsheet to Marta so we can reassign work before the intake call.

lee-ic: Thank you — appreciate the cover and keeping things confidential. 2pm PT intake works for me.

marta-peopleops: Invite sent to Kevin/Diego/Lee. Notes from the intake and any decisions will be recorded only in the PeopleOps case file. Please avoid replies here with medical specifics. :lock:
